d: Singapore is challenging London and New York’s dominance of the global gold trade. The city-state has launched a new gold custody service for foreign central banks and financial institutions, with a facility capable of storing up to 500 tonnes of bullion. In this video, Firstpost examines why Singapore wants to become a major gold hub, how Asia’s growing demand is driving the push and the incentives being offered to attract the industry. It also looks at the competition from Hong Kong, the changing way central banks manage their gold reserves and the geopolitical concerns behind the shift.…
